metadata.displayName: Ask questions about your own documents
metadata.description: Upload a folder of documents and get an endpoint that answers questions about them, quoting the passages it used. Your documents stay inside your own project and are deleted with it. You get your own kubeconfig, so you can inspect everything the platform runs for you.

parameters.name: projectName
parameters.label: Project name
parameters.help: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. This becomes the name of your cluster and your endpoint, and it cannot be changed afterwards.

parameters.name: baseModel
parameters.label: Model that answers the questions
parameters.help: Reads the passages found in your documents and writes the answer. Chosen from the models the platform team has reviewed.

parameters.name: embeddingModel
parameters.label: How your documents are indexed
parameters.help: Turns your documents into something searchable. This runs inside your project on CPU — it does not use a GPU and does not need its own endpoint. It cannot be changed later without rebuilding the index.

parameters.name: vectorDb
parameters.label: Search index
parameters.help: Qdrant, run for you inside your project. Nothing to configure.

parameters.name: corpusUploadId
parameters.label: Your documents
parameters.help: Markdown or plain-text files. They are copied into your project once, at setup, and deleted when the project is. If you leave this empty we index a small sample so you can see how it works.

parameters.name: topK
parameters.label: How many passages to use
parameters.help: How many passages are retrieved per question. More is slower and not always better.

parameters.name: availability
parameters.label: Availability
parameters.help: Always on answers immediately but holds a GPU the whole time. On demand frees the GPU when nobody is asking — your search index stays up, but the first question after a quiet spell waits about 15 seconds for the model to wake.

values.label: Always on
values.description: Answers immediately, day or night. Holds a GPU the whole time, whether or not anyone is asking questions.

values.label: On demand
values.description: Frees the GPU when nobody is asking. Your search index stays up, but the first question after a quiet spell waits about 15 seconds for the model to wake.

parameters.name: tier
parameters.label: Size
parameters.help: How much of the shared hardware your project may use at once. Both sizes are one GPU on this local rehearsal cluster.

parameters.name: durationDays
parameters.label: How long do you need it?
parameters.help: Your project — including your uploaded documents and the search index built from them — is removed automatically when this runs out. Ask for an extension if you need longer.
